summary:
SPE-5715 SYSTEMS companion (parent SPE-4792): implements and exposes graph_heartbeat and coord_drift_scan against the agent-substrate MCP server. Discovery first established that neither tool exists anywhere in programming-desk's own docs, contracts or gateway code (zero grep hits repo-wide; docs/upgrade-plan-desk-v2.md's 13-tool substrate list omits both; infra/lease-heartbeat/{LEASE-HEARTBEAT,DRIFT-SCAN}.md describe both as unresolved SYSTEMS work), matching the independent conclusion already recorded in draft PR #58 (LEAD). The ticket requester then confirmed verbatim signatures and the DriftKind enum from swcstudiospace/agent-substrate@main (packages/mcp-server/src/mcp.ts, lease.ts, drift.ts; SPE-4792 #6) outside this session's repo-scoped GitHub access (swcstudiospace/programming-desk only) — those signatures are implemented here as given, not independently re-derived against agent-substrate itself. Ships: systems.graph_heartbeat and systems.drift_scan backends calling Substrate.call_tool; a new contracts/tool-packs/coordination.yaml (seats: [systems]) rather than a direct contracts/tool-rosters/systems.yaml addition for the two tools, because that roster was already at 14 of the 15-tool ROSTER_MAX_TOOLS ceiling and both together would have pushed it to 16 (same fix as the SPE-5160/5161 android/ios precedent); one small additive edit to systems.yaml itself (desk_app_tools_load + packs_allowed: true, 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0, to exactly 15/15) since SYSTEMS could not load any pack at all without it; the companion contracts/changes/*.yaml document covering all four touched contract-surface files; and a drive-by fix to two pre-existing, already-stale hardcoded tool-pack-list assertions (test_server.py::test_health, test_units.py::test_rosters_load_from_contracts) in files this change already touches — both were failing on origin/main before this branch, from the SPE-5160/5161 pack additions, and are now computed from each pack file's own `app:` field instead. Deliberately not shipped: skills/desk-bootstrap/desk-production-loop/** (LEAD-owned) wiring of claim -> optional drift_scan -> work -> heartbeat -> complete/handoff — flagged in the change document as LEAD/QUALITY follow-up against this contract once it merges, not written here under ownership bot-01 does not have. PR #58 (LEAD, SPE-5715 gap report, draft) is left untouched.

Second round, addressing Greptile review on PR #59: (1) graph_heartbeat (both systems.py and a new lead.graph_state heartbeat action) now unwraps the substrate's content and fails closed on ok:false (lost/expired/unheld) instead of reporting a rejected renewal as ok:true. (2) lead.graph_state gains a fourth action, heartbeat (lease_id-authenticated, additive, lead.yaml 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0, stays at 15/15), because LEAD already holds claim/release/complete for a node and the SYSTEMS-only pack otherwise left it unable to renew a lease it claimed; coordination_drift_scan is deliberately NOT extended to LEAD, whose roster is already full — flagged as an open LEAD/QUALITY roster trade-off, not silently dropped. (3) coordination-drift-smoke.py now registers the graph/node before claiming it and treats every post-opt-in failure as FAIL rather than SKIP or a soft NOTE, and filters case (b)'s findings on graph_id and node_id together so they cannot match an unrelated graph's "n1". (4) the contract-change document gained contracts/tool-rosters/lead.yaml as a declared surface and dropped the explicit consumers_required override so G-4 resolves the full union from both rosters' contract_consumers entries instead of only the pack's. (5) test_server.py gained mocked-substrate coverage (success and rejection) for coordination_graph_heartbeat, coordination_drift_scan and the new lead heartbeat action — previously only the no-upstream fails-open/fails-closed paths were covered. (6) replied on PR #59 rather than fixing: a review comment asking for concurrent-claim (case a) exclusivity coverage here, since that is PR #58's lease-cas-drift-smoke.py and out of this change's stated scope (cases b/c only).

claims.claim: systems.py (graph_heartbeat, drift_scan) and the new smoke script both parse as valid Python 3
coordination.yaml and the new change document both parse as valid YAML
G-7 passes with the new coordination pack and the updated systems.yaml: 7 rosters, 8 packs (coordination added), systems.yaml at exactly 15/15 effective tools

G-1 passes for bot-01-systems-backend over this branch's full diff; the three contract-surface files touched (coordination.yaml, systems.yaml, the change document) are flagged as a NOTE requiring G-4, not a FOREIGN failure — no file outside bot-01's or the contract-surface carve-out's ownership is touched
G-4 passes: the change document declares both touched contract surfaces (surface + surfaces), resolves consumers, and is non-breaking with semantic_changes: []
G-3 (secret scan) finds nothing across all seven touched/added files
the full desk-gateway suite (104 tests, including the new coordination pack test and the two drive-by fixes to pre-existing stale pack-list assertions) passes with no regressions

the opt-in live smoke for drift-scan cases (b)/(c) skip-cleans with exit 0 and a printed reason when DESK_COORD_SMOKE_LIVE/SUBSTRATE_URL/SUBSTRATE_TOKEN are unset, per the agreed q2 default — it was not run live in this session (no substrate-mcp available here)

second round (Greptile review fixes): G-1 still passes with contracts/tool-rosters/lead.yaml and services/desk-gateway/src/desk_gateway/tools/lead.py added to the diff — 10 files, all within bot-01's or the contract-surface carve-out's ownership

second round: G-4 still passes with four declared contract surfaces (coordination.yaml, systems.yaml, lead.yaml, the change document itself) and no explicit consumers_required override, so the consumer list is resolved from both rosters' contract_consumers entries
second round: G-3 (secret scan) finds nothing across all ten touched/added files, including the two new tools/lead.py and tools/__init__.py edits

second round: the full desk-gateway suite is now 110 tests (6 new: mocked-substrate success/rejection coverage for coordination_graph_heartbeat, coordination_drift_scan, and the new lead.graph_state heartbeat action, plus its missing-lease_id guard) and passes with no regressions

second round: the rewritten smoke (graph_register before claim, FAIL instead of SKIP/NOTE on every post-opt-in problem, graph_id+node_id-filtered findings) still skip-cleans correctly with exit 0 when not opted in — its live path itself remains unexercised in this session, see unverified

unverified: graph_heartbeat and coord_drift_scan signatures, and the DriftKind enum, were not independently confirmed against swcstudiospace/agent-substrate by this session (out of this session's repo-scoped GitHub access); they are implemented exactly as given by the ticket requester and are only as reliable as that confirmation.

coordination-drift-smoke.py cases (b) and (c) have never been run against a live substrate-mcp in this session; only the skip-clean path (no live env) was exercised. The script's live path (claim, sleep past TTL, scan, scan with a fabricated git_tip, release) is untested beyond local syntax parsing.

no live call to coordination_graph_heartbeat, coordination_drift_scan or the new lead.graph_state heartbeat action through the deployed gateway process; coverage is the local pytest suite against both an unconfigured (not_configured) Substrate stub and a monkeypatched Substrate.call_tool returning hand-written success/rejection bodies shaped like the agent-substrate signatures as given — not a real substrate response.

the production-loop skill wiring (claim -> optional drift_scan -> work -> heartbeat -> complete/handoff) is not implemented in this change; it is LEAD-owned (skills/desk-bootstrap/desk-production-loop/**) and is flagged in the change document as a follow-up, not fabricated here under ownership bot-01 does not have.

LEAD still cannot reach coordination_drift_scan (only the new heartbeat action on its existing desk_graph_state): LEAD's roster is already at the 15-tool ROSTER_MAX_TOOLS ceiling, so giving it desk_app_tools_load to load the coordination pack means retiring one of LEAD's other six tools — a roster trade-off this change does not make unilaterally. Flagged in the change document as an open LEAD/QUALITY decision.

no QUALITY acknowledgement has been collected yet for the contract change (acknowledgements: [] — informational only since the change is non-breaking); consumers_required is no longer set explicitly, so G-4 resolves it from ownership.yaml's contract_consumers for both contracts/tool-packs/** and contracts/tool-rosters/** — not independently re-verified against a human sign-off.
